name: Post-Sabbatical Talk - Dr. Katherine Perry
description: In this talk, I will introduce the fields of graph theory and network science, highlighting how networks can be used to model and analyze relationships in a wide variety of settings. I will share some of my work from sabbatical, including recent joint work with Hiroshi Nonaka ('26) on using network analysis to study character interactions in AI-generated short stories. My hope is to introduce these tools to a broad audience and inspire others to consider how network science might be applied in their own research.

name: Meet the Author: Dr. Shane Barter
description: This presentation celebrates the release of Partial Sovereignty: The Politics of Autonomy among Minority Nations (UBC Press) in Fall 2026. The book focuses on the meaning, forms, and dangers of territorial autonomy – special self-government for minority nations. Cases span Western democracies (Quebec, Catalonia), conflict resolution (Northern Ireland, Aceh), authoritarianism (Chechnya, Tibet), and Indigenous self-government (Nunavut, Guna Yala). It argues that autonomy has never resulted in independence, and by recognizing minority nations, helps to maintain territorial borders. The presentation provides an overview of the book and the process of writing it, including global fieldwork, numerous conferences, and many Soka research assistants.

name: Tech Coast Angels: Face-to-Face with Investors| REAL WORLD SHARK TANK!
Tech Coast Angels | Face to Face With Investors
description:
Most students don't get in a room with active angel investors until years into a career — if ever. This one's on your own campus.

B2B is bringing Face to Face with Investors to Soka, a signature round-table networking event hosted by TCA Venture Group that puts early-stage founders directly across the table from active local investors. Whether you're already building something, have an idea you've been sitting on, or just want to understand how funding conversations actually happen, this is the room to be in.

What to Expect

Round-Table Conversations — Direct, small-group discussions and Q&As with active angel investors. No pitch competition, no stage — just real conversation.

- Real-Time Feedback — Constructive advice on your idea, your vision, and how you'd approach fundraising, from people who fund startups for a living.

- Ecosystem Networking — Connect with fellow founders, university entrepreneurship centers, and regional startup leaders — the kind of network that outlasts a single event.

- Industry Breakouts — Focused conversations across sectors including AI, life sciences, consumer products, software, and general markets — there's a table for wherever your interest lies.

Why it matters: access like this usually isn't available to undergrads, let alone on their own campus. Come with a question, a rough idea, or just curiosity — you'll leave with a real conversation under your belt and a few new names in your network.

name: Traditional Medicine: An Interdisciplinary Exploration
description: Join Professor Michael Golden, Dr. Hung Phan, and Dr. Chika Esiobu for a conversation on traditional medicine from several angles. Professor Golden will look at cultures that still practice healing through traditional music, and at the beliefs they hold about how music restores health and wholeness. Dr. Phan will show how computational chemistry and machine learning can help reveal how the molecules in traditional remedies work. Dr. Esiobu will cover the latest global action on traditional medicine from the World Health Organization and other stakeholders.

name: Asian Americas: Discussing Papers from Graduate Students at CalState Los Angeles
description: Co-sponsored by the Pacific Basin Area and the Pacific Basin Research Center, this conference will bring two CalState Los Angeles graduate students focusing on Asian migrant communities to share their research with undergraduates, particularly students in the Intro to the Pacific Basin course. SUA students will serve as discussants before concluding the evening with a cafeteria dinner to discuss graduate studies in Los Angeles. The presentations feature Ari Muramoto examining how Guadalajara’s Chinese community contradicted Mexico's antichinismo movement through local integration and resistance to the California borderlands model, and Henry Truong utilizing oral histories to document a Vietnamese refugee family's resettlement and business establishment in a rural California desert and military town.

name: Richard Marx
description:
Richard Marx is a GRAMMY-winning singer, songwriter, and producer whose career has spanned four decades of chart success and creative reinvention. With over 45 million albums sold, one billion streams, and fourteen No. 1 singles to his name (including “Right Here Waiting,” “Hazard” & “Hold On to the Nights”), Marx is the only male artist in history to have his first seven singles reach the Top 5 on the Billboard charts, and one of only two artists—alongside Michael Jackson—to write a No. 1 song in four different decades. Marx’s work extends far beyond his own recordings, having written and produced for artists including Luther Vandross, Keith Urban, NSYNC, Barbra Streisand and Burt Bacharach.
